title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference | Week 4 vs. New York Giants
headline: LaFleur praised Trey McBride's run-game blocking and said Max Melton and Denzel Burke responded well to bigger roles, while Walter Nolen still needs to produce more inside.
summary: LaFleur spent much of the session on the evolution of tight end play, arguing that defenses sitting in shells and teams avoiding big-on-big matchups have pushed offenses toward running and short passing. He praised Trey McBride as an elite pass catcher who also holds up in the run game because of his mindset and detail. On the defensive side, he said Max Melton and Denzel Burke responded about as well as expected in their expanded roles last week and that he has confidence in the group. He said Walter Nolen wants to help the team badly but needs to keep improving, and he noted that no one had sacked Brock Purdy this year. Looking ahead to the New York Giants, LaFleur described their front seven as loaded, said they are a sharp schematic operation, and noted that Brian Burns is out. He also said the offense is still developing after three weeks, that the team needs to fix pre-snap penalties, and that the defense has to keep mixing up its looks. He was skeptical about bringing back defensive pass interference challenges.

signals.note: Praise for his blocking suggests he stays a full-time, every-down tight end and keeps his volume steady regardless of matchup.

signals.note: A positive review of his expanded role supports keeping him in a larger defensive role going forward.
signals.quote: I thought they responded well.

He said pre-snap penalties are the issue to fix, placing the responsibility on the whole staff and team, and said he won't limit players' aggressive play style.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses Lamar Jackson, Facing the Titans
headline: Lamar Jackson was limited in practice with a minor issue, while centers Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic are out long term and Andrew Vorhees and Emery Jones are competing for the interior line spot.
summary: Minter said Lamar Jackson was limited at practice and was dealing with something small, and he was glad Jackson got meaningful work in after reports that he had been absent earlier. He framed the week around the team controlling what it can control and playing cleanly in all three phases, with the Titans as a respected but secondary focus. On Titans QB Cam Ward, he cited his talent and said Ward's rookie year was disrupted by multiple play callers and a head-coaching change, and that he now has an established coordinator in Brian Daboll. Minter called Tennessee much improved, with a strong interior defensive line, two good backs, and young weapons on the outside. On the offensive line, he said Gwyn and Pocic are long-term absences, and the team is using in-house options at center for this game, with a longer-term group to be settled over a week or two. At guard, Vorhees has experience and Emery Jones has developed through camp, so the team will let them compete. On defense, he said the tackling issue needs to be solved through technique and confidence, and the unit must improve both scheme and effort at the point of attack. He also said defensive pass interference replay is a question for the offseason, and he praised Nate Wiggins for his response after a disputed play.

title: Joe Brady On Team Intensity, Facing The Patriots, And More
headline: James Cook is trending up as Buffalo's lead back, while CB Christian Benford's toe injury remains an open question for this week.
summary: Coach Joe Brady said he is not concerned about QB Josh Allen's condition, describing the 'banged up' label as normal wear the day after games. He framed the Patriots' blitz-heavy approach as a matchup of execution, saying the key is protecting the football and being ready for whatever New England shows. Brady said he doesn't care about division standings right now, stressing that every team is still figuring itself out and that the Bills must treat this game like any other. On ball security, he said it is fully coachable, down to the details of contact and carrying technique. He praised RB James Cook for making the most of growing opportunities, noting that Cook bounced back from a rough first play to have a strong game. Brady said the run defense is growing and has seen three different run schemes, though some runs still need better attacking and fitting. On Christian Benford, Brady said the toe injury will be monitored through the week, and that some players sitting out Wednesday may still play Sunday. He said DL Phidarian Mathis, who was unfortunately sidelined, is back in the building and working with the strength staff, and that Mathis will play if he has the opportunity.

title: Dave Canales encourages fans to wear black on Sunday
headline: Bryce Young (knee soreness) practiced fully and is expected to play; Monroe Freeling (concussion protocol) is trending up but not cleared; Xavier Legette is week to week; Jaycee Horn and Michael Jackson are on IR with roughly 6 to 8 week timelines.
summary: Canales said Monroe Freeling is trending in the right direction after being diagnosed with concussion symptoms following the game. He entered the protocol the morning after and was moving around but not cleared for practice, with hopes he practices Tuesday. Bryce Young finished the game despite a sore knee, is getting heavy treatment, and went through full-speed work in individual and team periods, so Canales is confident he'll be ready. Corey Bullock is expected to play guard for Damien Lewis, who has an elbow issue and needs about a week, with Canales mentioning Week 6 against Philadelphia as a possible return. Akayleb Evans finished the game at corner, plays coverage units, and had a strong camp. Canales said Xavier Legette is more week to week and Jalen Coker moved well but must prove he can play football before he's cleared. On the IR players, Michael Jackson had successful groin surgery and has an optimistic six-week timeline, while Jaycee Horn is non-surgical, in rehab, with an estimated eight weeks give or take. Canales attributed the defensive soft-tissue injuries to heavy snap counts and high-speed mileage over three games, and said the walkthrough was about getting five or so guys physical reps while limiting tempo.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “It’s Going to Turn” | Press Conference
headline: Jaishawn Barham is locked in as the starting Mike linebacker, Javonte Williams and the run game are trending up, and Malachi Lawrence is set to see more snaps as Dallas prepares for Houston.
summary: Schottenheimer said the Cowboys made roster moves ahead of Houston: Jonathan Bullard and Jalen Thompson go to IR, Elijah Garcia moves to the active roster, and three players were added to the practice squad. Overshown and Malik Hooker are ramping up from injury, with Hooker seen as slightly closer, and the staff will know more after practice. He praised Javonte Williams and the run game, saying the team got more explosive plays and that it had been too cute early in the season. He said Barham has earned the middle linebacker opportunity and that the green dot helps settle him in, while noting the job will be shared by a rotating group. On the pass rush, he wants more production from the interior line of Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, and he plans to trim snaps from Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku to give Malachi Lawrence more work. He said Dak Prescott and he are fine on in-game communication, and that Prescott's ball distribution to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens has been strong. He expects Nico Collins back for Houston and called the Texans' defensive front very talented, while stressing the team is focused on itself and that it believes things will turn.

title: HC Sean Payton on continuing to find ways to improve: ‘We’re early in this race'
headline: Payton says J.K. Dobbins practiced in full after a postgame boot and the team must start faster and run the ball in the first half.
summary: Payton said the Broncos have to start faster, since they have been poor in the first half of all three games and have not run the ball consistently in those halves. He called their first-half scoring and point-differential rankings unacceptable and said the staff is building scenarios to get early takeaways. He praised the 49ers' Brock Purdy for playing decisively with no sacks allowed and efficient numbers on early downs. On J.K. Dobbins, Payton said he is ready, that the team re-signed him for his skill set and competitiveness, and that he practiced fully on Wednesday despite the boot he wore after the last game. Payton also said the team wants more turnovers forced and fewer offensive turnovers, and that it is too early to read much into a league-wide rise in defensive blitz rates. He said the team's depth at linebacker is good, and he reflected on Christian McCaffrey's move to San Francisco as a strong fit with Kyle Shanahan's system.

title: Campbell on Goff & Gill-Howard
headline: Campbell says Goff's cerebral game is the offense's engine, Gill-Howard earned offensive snaps, and the 2024 class (Rakestraw, Mahogany) must help take load off Gibbs.
summary: Campbell previewed Sunday night's road game in Charlotte against Carolina, calling it a loud environment and a good opponent coming off a loss. He praised the Panthers' defense as sound and aggressive, led by a front that includes Brown and Phillips, and said Lloyd is expected back. He flagged their QB Bryce as quick-releasing and their run game and big receivers and tight ends as tests. On the offensive line, he said the unit played much better against the Jets and Buffalo, with Blake Miller back, Mahogany playing well, and Juice Scruggs settling in at center. He defended Goff's mobility as a non-issue, comparing his cerebral style to Brady, Manning and Brees. Campbell said rookie Skyler Gill-Howard earned offensive snaps through urgency and effort. He described Goff as tough and durable, a captain who plays through things without missing practice. On the 2024 class, he said Rakestraw, Mahogany and a third young player can elevate the offense and take some load off Gibbs. He called Blake Miller consistent and steady for a young tackle who has taken lumps. He also said he is fine with DPI no longer being challengeable.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Nico Collins’ Return & Texans vs Cowboys
headline: Nico Collins is back practicing but his Week 4 status is still undetermined, Azeez Al-Shaair is week-to-week with a groin injury, and the defense has lost Mario Edwards for the season.
summary: Ryans said Nico Collins is back at practice and is a true threat whenever he's on the field, though he will wait to see how the week goes before confirming Sunday. Azeez Al-Shaair has a groin injury and will be week to week, which puts more pressure on young linebackers such as Jake Hansen and Wade Woodaz, whom Ryans said must simply play their roles and communicate. Ryans called the loss of Mario Edwards, who brought intensity and pass-rush ability, a tough blow, and said he will miss the rest of the season. He praised Reed Blankenship's progress from Week 1 to Week 3 and said Kenneth Murray is picking up the verbiage well. On offense, Ryans said the run game needs to be reset around aiming points, hat placement and back tracks, and that Ed Ingram's return should help the line's physicality. He also said motion has been productive and that the offense must stay efficient on early downs. Defensively, the middle issues come down to tackling after checkdowns, not personnel. Ryans framed the Cowboys game as a big moment for the franchise's 25th anniversary and the fans, and he expects a loud crowd.

title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts vs. Commanders
headline: Alec Pierce is out for now and Daniel Jones is playing well, while Ashton Dulin's travel status to London is still unclear.
summary: Steichen says the Colts are excited for the Thursday trip to London to face the Commanders, a well-coached team coming off a win over Seattle. He expects Washington's quarterback to be either Jayden Daniels or Marcus Mariota, both mobile, so the Colts must set strong rush lanes and coverage regardless. He describes Washington's defense as very multiple with frequent pressure and blitzes, and notes its coordinator came from Minnesota. On the travel plan, the team will try to stay on East Coast time and keep its schedule, and Steichen calls the Thursday-night trip a proven approach from past overseas games. He calls Stefon Diggs and Terry McLaurin explosive and says the Colts must limit their big plays by tracking their alignments and routes. On Daniel Jones, Steichen says he is completing close to 70% and should keep getting stronger as the season goes on, while the team focuses on protecting the ball in the pocket. He says losing Alec Pierce for now hurts the offense and that the staff must create chunk plays through scheme and favorable looks. Ashton Dulin is progressing well but his travel status is still undecided, and the team is working through which injured players will make the trip.

title: Liam Coen on Team Mentality Entering Week 4, Continuing to Respond | Press Conference
headline: Coen says Chris Rodriguez Jr. gained confidence and better run lanes in Week 3, and credits year-two continuity for fewer self-inflicted penalties.
summary: Coen said the team's penalty discipline has improved in year two because players are running the same system on both sides of the ball, and he stressed that the group must stay disciplined and consistent over a long season. He praised Parker Washington's contested-catch ability and fearlessness at the catch point, saying the trait can't be coached and that Trevor Lawrence trusts him in critical situations. On the Bengals, he described Cincinnati's defense as patient and disruptive, with Dexter Lawrence drawing multiple gaps, and said Joe Burrow's accuracy and ability to extend plays are what make him dangerous. He said the message this week is about responding to adversity and focusing on the next play. Coen said he supports bringing back defensive pass interference challenges in critical moments. title: Kirk Cousins on Klint Kubiak: 'Nothing is going to get past his watchful eye'
headline: Cousins praises Brock Bowers' after-the-catch ability and says the chemistry with him is still developing ahead of the Chiefs game.
summary: Quarterback Kirk Cousins spoke ahead of Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. He called head coach Klint Kubiak organized and detail-oriented, saying the play calls come in quickly and that Kubiak stays focused on coaching even after wins. Cousins said he has worked with Kubiak since their time together in 2019 and 2020 and in 2021, and he finds comfort in that. On Brock Bowers, he called the tight end very capable, with tremendous after-the-catch ability, good hands, and strong play strength, along with the intelligence and work ethic he brings. He said the on-field chemistry between them is still being built, noting they have not had as many reps together as he would like. He compared it to his earlier work with Justin Jefferson and Adam Thielen, where years of reps made the timing feel automatic. On the running game, Cousins said the offense needs to get it going, and that the coaching staff will stay committed to it and expects it to improve as the season goes on. He credited the defense for short fields in recent wins and framed team success as a shared effort. He also described Patrick Mahomes as a standard for quarterback play, and said no lead feels safe against the Chiefs.

On injuries, he said Justin Jefferson (ankle sprain), Chuck Demmings and Brett Thorson will not practice today, and he is listing Jefferson as day-to-day, feeling better but not yet cleared. He said the offense struggled to adjust after Jefferson left the Tampa game, and he took responsibility for not adjusting well enough. He said the team is running the ball a lot, is seeing more eight-man fronts, and wants to keep leaning on the run game, with Aaron Jones carrying a big load while Jordan Mason is out. He said he wants Demond Claiborne involved more in the backfield, and that Claiborne has already helped on special teams. On Kyler Murray, he said they are working on under-center and pistol concepts to improve rhythm and protection. He also said Gavin Bartholomew's snap count will go up as he takes on more of Josh Oliver's role, with T.J. Hockenson leading the tight end group.

title: Drake Maye on Mike Vrabel 9/30: "I love playing for him, that's not going to change"
headline: Maye says his shoulder isn't affecting his throwing and blames turnovers and decision-making for the offense's problems; Romeo Doubs is earning more trust.
summary: Drake Maye pushed back on reports of a rift with Mike Vrabel, calling him one of the best coaches he's had and saying his enjoyment of playing for him won't change. Asked about his shoulder, he said it hasn't affected his throwing or decision-making, and that he felt good at practice. He said the offense isn't struggling to move the ball; the problem is turnovers and mistakes that stall drives before touchdowns. He added that he has made throws and decisions he wishes he could take back, and that the team needs to trust its line and playmakers. On the upcoming game at Buffalo, he described the Bills as well coached, disciplined, and hard to move the ball against, and noted the new stadium and their explosive offense. He said the Bills' defense under Jim Leonard uses similar concepts to the Sean McDermott staff but mixes in different personnel and tests opponents' strengths. He praised Romeo Doubs' growing trust, blocking, and work ethic, and called fullback Reggie Gilliam one of the best at his position and very smart. He also said the team won't simplify the offense, since the core of what they do is already established. On ball security, he said the running back ball-protection drills were reinforced with the running backs coach, and he emphasized holding the ball tighter.

He acknowledged the goal-line sequence was a poor play design and execution problem and said he still has faith in that play. title: Todd Bowles on Jalon Daniels: Up to the Challenge | Press Conference
headline: Jalon Daniels makes his first NFL start on the road Thursday vs. Green Bay; David Walker is set for more snaps with Rueben Bain's status unresolved, and Sean Tucker should get more carries.
summary: Bowles said the team is still deciding on Rueben Bain, who will be evaluated at the end of the week, and that the shoulder remains a concern. Josiah Trotter did everything in practice and will be evaluated again once shoulder pads go on. Bowles said Daniels' preparation for the first start is mostly film work and mental readiness, and he stressed that Daniels should do his job without trying to do too much. He said the offensive line breakdowns were a team-wide issue involving backs, communication, footwork and fundamentals, and that practice changes had been made. Bowles praised Daniels' calm demeanor and pocket play, and said the offense will be tailored to him, though Baker Mayfield's greater experience allowed more mental load and checks. He described Green Bay's offense as explosive, led by Jordan Love and Tucker Kraft. On the backfield, he said Sean Tucker needs to run the ball more, and on the defensive line he said David Walker has earned more snaps, particularly with Bain out. He also said the team needs to use Antoine Winfield Jr. more to get his playmaking into the game.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh says Cam Ward's footwork is improving but downfield shots remain limited; John Franklin-Myers (back) sat Wednesday, and Pollard and Spears were also out, with the coach not overly concerned about Sunday.
summary: Saleh opened with an injury update: John Franklin-Myers is dealing with a back issue and sat Wednesday, and Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears were also out, though he is not overly concerned about any of them for Sunday. He said a player needs surgery and will be out for the rest of the year, but declined to say who will fill that spot or whether Pat Coogan would play guard or center. On Cam Ward, Saleh said his footwork and pocket presence are lasting longer into games and he is trusting the offensive line more, though he sometimes reverts to old habits late. He credited the staff and Ward's work ethic and expects the mechanics to stop being a topic eventually. Saleh said slow starts come from a mix of factors, including a fumbled opening kickoff, dropped passes, and defensive stops that didn't happen, and that the team's young group is getting better. He defended the offense's shot selection against two-high defenses, saying Ward has to be selective and take what defenses give, and said the team opened things up by running the ball in the second half. He praised JC Latham's season and said the new starter next to him has communicated well. He also said Ward and coordinator Daboll are communicating well while still learning a new system, and that a Baltimore game plan will focus on disciplined pass rush against Lamar Jackson's scrambling.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/30/26
headline: Jayden Daniels is limited to jog-through work with a return-to-play timeline; he is not ruled out for Sunday, with a decision expected by Friday.
summary: Quinn said Daniels is starting a limited, jog-level return-to-play process and will gradually get more team reps through Thursday and Friday before a Friday determination. He described him as a shot to play Sunday but said it is too early to call, and that the brace he will wear the whole season is a big part of the process. Quinn said Rachaad White is still dealing with a shoulder injury and needs more treatment, so he is not practicing today. Percy Butler is still in concussion protocol but will participate today. Samuel Cosmi and Nick Cross stayed behind in London-area prep rather than traveling, with the aim of getting them back next week. On Austin Ekeler, Quinn said he is not yet on the field fully, is learning a new system, and will be evaluated over about three days on his response to workload and readiness. Lucas Patrick is limited but Quinn liked what he saw inside at center, and the best-five combinations are still being worked out. On the linebackers, Frankie Luvu's return would be a big boost, and Sonny Styles and others will share the work. In the secondary, Mike Sainristil moved to nickel and has been featured, with Fabian Moreau getting added reps alongside Rasul Douglas.
